W3 (cost lens), after E028.

**Tip (E027).** 8.75 true epochs (219 steps at batch 2000), with resolution phases of 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30% of steps. It measured 5.878 s at 0.7547 on seeds 0–2, but its held-out mean is 0.7526, so the population mean is below the 0.753 bar.

**Time budget.** Time ≈ 0.55 s fixed plus about 5.3 s of pixel-weighted step cost. Moving 15% of steps from 24 px to 20 px buys about 0.17–0.18 s (E026).

**Best lever so far.** E028 tested FreezeOut on group 1. It saved 0.84 s (−13.5%) for about 0.2 pp on seeds 0–2. That is about 4 s/pp, the best exchange rate measured so far. Truncation-style cuts are therefore the strongest time lever, but only if a time-neutral booster first restores about 0.3 pp.

**Boosters.** Every hyperparameter booster tried so far came back within noise: LS, wd, lr, Muon lr and the alpha exponent. My prior for each remaining one (warm-up, Lookahead interval, LS tail, per-resolution whitening) is about +0.0 to 0.1 pp.

**Noise.** The step count stays the same for these ideas, so seeds 0–2 give a paired comparison on the same RNG stream. The 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp, and time noise is about 0.5–1%.

forecasts.reason: Schedule-shape knobs have all been flat so far, and Lookahead averaging follows the peak, so a gain of at least 0.2 pp is unlikely and time does not change.
Halving the number of Lookahead updates saves almost no time. E025 suggests averaging is near its optimum, and rescaling alpha keeps the pull per step the same, so I expect noise or a slight loss.
Setting LS to 0 for the tail may sharpen the logits slightly, but LS changes so far have been flat. Any effect will be under 0.15 pp and unresolvable.
This repeats E026's swap of 33 steps from 24 to 20 px, which should save about 0.17 s (3%). The accuracy cost is about 0.1–0.2 pp, which lands right at the 0.752 held-out gate.
The extra eigh calls in prepare cost about 0.02–0.05 s. BN after the stem already absorbs most of the scale mismatch, so the gain is likely at most 0.1 pp.

cruxes: What is E028's (FreezeOut) held-out seeds 3–12 mean? If its loss is 0.2 pp or less, it buys about 0.8 s at about 4 s/pp. It should then be stacked with a 0.25-epoch add-back instead of hunting for boosters.

Does any time-neutral booster deliver at least +0.2 pp held-out? If none does, every further time cut has to be paid for by adding epochs back, and FreezeOut or early low resolution are the only cheaper currencies.
Is the 20 px phase really close to free (I050)? If extending it costs at most 0.1 pp, early low resolution reaches about 2 s/pp or better and can be pushed further.
